findings.description: While the conductor runs, `needOf` drops every `awaiting-review` session. That includes one where the conductor's `pup merge --pr` was refused on a soft flag. The session stays `awaiting-review` until the operator approves debt, and the PR's premise that the operator's turn "comes back as the `pr-open` line" never happens for it.
findings.body:
**A session whose `--pr` gate was refused disappears from every operator surface while the conductor runs.**

The new check removes the need for any `awaiting-review` session whenever `snapshot.conductor.running` is true:

```ts
  if (session.state === 'awaiting-review' && !gating) {
```

<https://github.com/AlexisBalayre/pupitre/blob/ff930ed212da4c953b12a0cf8cc102764f6b278b/src/core/dashboard.service.ts#L446-L455>

The conductor does not get every such session to a PR:

- **A refused gate leaves the session where it was.** On a soft flag (`flaggedDebt.length > 0 && !req.acceptDebt`), `refuseGate` appends a `gate_result` event `{ outcome: 'refused', report }` and returns `status: 'refused'`. It never transitions the session ([merge-gate.service.ts#L1574-L1583](https://github.com/AlexisBalayre/pupitre/blob/ff930ed212da4c953b12a0cf8cc102764f6b278b/src/core/merge-gate.service.ts#L1574-L1583)). `MergeStatus` documents that the session "stays in awaiting-review (a human decides)" ([merge-gate.types.ts#L59-L66](https://github.com/AlexisBalayre/pupitre/blob/ff930ed212da4c953b12a0cf8cc102764f6b278b/src/core/types/merge-gate.types.ts#L59-L66)).
- **The conductor cannot make that call.** Its prompt says "You relay an approval, you never give one" ([profile-compiler.service.ts#L871-L892](https://github.com/AlexisBalayre/pupitre/blob/ff930ed212da4c953b12a0cf8cc102764f6b278b/src/core/profile-compiler.service.ts#L871-L892)), and decision 75 requires a named human approver. So no PR is opened and no `pr-open` line ever appears.
- **Other `--pr` refusals strand it the same way.** One example is a missing push target (`merge-gate.service.ts` ~L820). A session the operator launched while the conductor window is up is also affected, because the conductor only gates the sessions it launched.

In each case nothing else in `needOf` catches the session. `question`, `blocked`, `top-rung` and `stalled` don't apply, `pr-open` needs a recorded PR, and `lastGate` is never read. So the session drops out of `pup status` Needs-you, `pup ui`, the terminal tab count and the web inbox, and remains only as a table row. Decision 102's claim that the operator's turn "comes back as the `pr-open` line once the gate opens the PR" does not hold here. No test covers a refused gate while the conductor runs.

**Fix direction:** keep the need when the session's newest `gate_result` event is a refusal.

- Compute something like `gateRefused` in `dashboardSession` from the latest `gate_result` event's `outcome === 'refused'`. `lastGate.passed === false` won't work, because it would match a stale rejection after a rerun.
- Change the condition to `session.state === 'awaiting-review' && (!gating || session.gateRefused)`.
- Ideally, give that case an answer that names `--accept-debt`.

findings.description: The new inline comment in `needOf` restates what this PR already added to the `needsYou` JSDoc (conductor gates awaiting-review, decision 102). `needOf` is private with one caller, and AGENTS.md says to delete a call-site copy the seam already states. Drop it or cut it to a bare decision pointer.

Decision 102 says the conductor gates its own branches from "decision 74 onward". Decision 74 is about keeping workers off AskUserQuestion/EnterPlanMode, and the conductor gate with `pup merge --pr` is decision 75, so this should read "decision 75 onward".

Decision 102 "Amends decision 83", but 83 still lists awaiting-review unconditionally with no `*Amended by decision 102:*` marker, which neighbouring amended entries carry (e.g. L328, L442, L3923, L5170).
Decision 97 still says iTerm2's `needs you` status fires when a session is awaiting review. With a conductor running that no longer holds after decision 102, and 102 does not mention amending 97.
